Cautiously positive macro tone from the FOMC (solid job gains, moderate growth, below-target inflation, gradualism with balance-sheet normalization “relatively soon”) is tempered by the latest Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey:

- Domestic banks report weaker demand across CRE (including construction, land development, and multifamily) and softer demand for consumer credit (autos and credit cards), with standards tightening for consumer, auto, and credit card loans. Demand for nonfarm nonresidential (C&I) loans is broadly unchanged.
- Residential real estate standards have eased (including jumbo, QM, and GSE segments), which supports housing, but this is offset by weakness in CRE demand.
- Foreign banks indicate tighter lending standards across C&I (small, middle, and large firms) and CRE, suggesting a modest drag from cross-border/intermediated credit supply.

FSR overlay remains: vulnerabilities moderate overall, but valuations elevated and nonfinancial business leverage higher—arguing for vigilance.

Implication: Credit conditions look mixed-to-soft versus earlier reads, which could modestly dampen the growth impulse even as monetary policy stays accommodative. Net assessment remains slightly positive but nudged down from prior.
